content.intro: In this lesson, you will study introduction to AI Model Evaluation within Model Evaluation, Validation, and Reliability. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Evaluation is part of system design, not an afterthought. A metric is useful only when it reflects the goal, data conditions, and error costs.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Evaluation tests a model or system against stated success criteria and realistic held-out examples. Select metrics that match the task and report limitations; fitting or a polished demo is not an adequate evaluation.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Identify what introduction to ai model evaluation takes as input and what result or decision it is intended to support. 2. Read the example before running it and predict the output. 3. Run the small example, compare actual and expected output, then change one input or assumption and repeat. 4. Record what the example demonstrates and what it does not demonstrate about a real system.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. Evaluation is part of system design, not an afterthought. A metric is useful only when it reflects the goal, data conditions, and error costs.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example. If the example runs as expected, do not infer that it proves a trained model works; this snippet is a deterministic teaching aid. Keep sensitive data out of tests.

content_blocks.title: Check before you trust a result
content_blocks.text: This is a small, deterministic teaching example—not a trained AI model or evidence of production performance. Run it with a local Python 3 interpreter; do not paste secrets or private data into experiments.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Evaluation tests a model or system against stated success criteria and realistic held-out examples. Select metrics that match the task and report limitations; fitting or a polished demo is not an adequate evaluation. Next, connect this lesson to its prerequisite or next lesson and carry the same habit forward: define success, test a representative case, inspect failures, and document limitations.

content.task: Try it yourself: build a tiny synthetic dataset for introduction to ai model evaluation, establish a simple baseline, and define a suitable metric before looking at results. Separate development decisions from final evaluation and describe one important error.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the core concept and accurately refer to the source syllabus topics.
Record a prediction and compare it with a reproducible result or a clearly stated manual trace.
Document at least one limitation, safety consideration, or evaluation requirement.
hints: Write down the inputs, expected output, and assumptions before changing the example.
Change only one input or condition and compare the results with your original prediction.
Ask whether the example covers realistic cases, important subgroups, and failure conditions; a toy example does not establish production reliability.
